Where it began

Danish Kaneria was born in Karachi on 16 December 1980. He went to St Patrick's High School in the city and later studied at the Government Islamia College. He was nicknamed Danny. Test cricket ran in the family: his cousin, Anil Dalpat, kept wicket for Pakistan.

His first-class career began in 1998–99, for National Shipping Corporation against HBL, with two wickets. Two years later he was a Test cricketer, a 19-year-old leg-spinner with a googly, making his debut against England at Faisalabad in November 2000.

The player

Kaneria played 61 Tests for Pakistan between 2000 and 2010 and took 261 wickets at 34.80. He took five in an innings 15 times and ten in a match twice, with a best of 7 for 77 against Bangladesh at Dhaka. By the end of his Test career no Pakistan spinner had taken more Test wickets, and only Wasim Akram, Waqar Younis and Imran Khan had taken more for Pakistan at all.

The good days came early. In the 2001–02 Asian Test Championship he took six in each innings against Bangladesh, 12 for 94, and was man of the match. Against South Africa at Lahore in 2003–04 he bowled 28.3 overs unchanged and earned the award again. In October 2004 he took ten against Sri Lanka at Karachi, sending down 60 overs in the second innings to set up a six-wicket win. At Sydney a few months later he took 7 for 188 against Australia, his hundredth Test wicket among them, and Shane Warne spoke highly of the effort.

What made him special

He gave his captain control as well as wickets. The South Africans at Lahore could never be sure which way he would turn it, and the BBC rated him a bowler who could win matches. Late in his career he helped Pakistan beat India, England and West Indies in Tests.

Batting was a gentler pursuit. He made 360 Test runs at 7.06, with a top score of 29, but he was not out 33 times, so he was at least hard to dislodge. One-day cricket brought 15 wickets in 18 matches, as Pakistan tended to pick spinners who could also bat, such as Shahid Afridi and Shoaib Malik.

Beyond the Tests

In England he bowled for Essex, and bowled well. In 2005 he took 32 wickets in seven Championship games, and in 2007 he took 107 for the county across all competitions. At home he played for a long line of sides, among them Karachi, Habib Bank, Sindh and the Karachi Zebras. In all first-class cricket he took 1,024 wickets in 206 matches, with a best of 8 for 59.

And finally

At Multan in November 2006, Brian Lara took 26 runs off one of his overs. Kaneria kept bowling and finished the innings with five wickets. That is the leg-spinner's craft in a sentence: you will be hit, so make sure you are the one smiling at the end.
